pages.text: Drop matter into a spinning black hole's ergosphere, split it so half falls in on a negative-energy orbit, and the other half escapes with more energy than you sent. The extra comes out of the hole's spin. Feed it angular momentum to keep it spinning.
$(thing)Set$(): Splitting radius r/M, Injection rate, Spin-up torque, Horizon field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Accretion torque noise: the spin-up torque varies by ±20%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Splitting point inside the horizon: nothing comes back; Outside the ergosphere: no negative-energy orbits exist; Interlock: horizon-threading coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the horizon-threading coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output scales with the extracted power.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Horizon radius r₊: r₊ = M + √(M² − a²)$(br)Maximum efficiency: η_max = ½(√(2M/r₊) − 1)$(br)Efficiency η: η ≈ η_max·(2M − r)/(2M − r₊)$(br)Penrose power: P = η·ṁc²$(br)Blandford-Znajek power: P_BZ ∝ a²B²$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)
